title: Scope Hyperliquid / trade.xyz accounts: cheaper or easier trading, new tradables, and live-money proxies for options/futures the fiat accounts cannot trade
note: [2026-11-15 08:26Z Manager 15a] Operator 2026-11-15 ~08:24Z, verbatim: "we were going to do some scoping to see if it was worth adding trading accounts for hyperliquid/trading xyz, either for easier/cheaper trading or new tradables we can't currently access - this could also help us respove some of the issues we have with fiat accounts we're we can't really trade options/futures on live money - perhaps there are proxies on one of those brokerages that are more easily tradable, like the cryptos we're trading today". Output: a scoping memo-as-evidence (a research/queue-style record): fee and funding stack vs bybit_2 net of the full cost stack; listed perps / tradables, especially equity-index, commodity and rates proxies (e.g. perps on SPX/NDX/gold/oil) mapped onto the legs we cannot trade live today (MES/MGC/MHG futures, options); API and order-type support (brackets, TP/SL amend) against our executor contract; custody, KYC and jurisdiction constraints; liquidity and slippage on the candidate symbols; the integration cost via the new-broker skill. Decision rule stated before reading: worth adding only if a candidate venue gives a rostered or Stage-0-passed leg a live-tradable instrument, or cuts realized cost on an existing leg by a measured margin. Credential steps are the operator's (originate keys only).
outcome: Operator 2026-11-23: not eligible (Hyperliquid terms restrict US persons) — 'we're not eligible, so we can drop that for now'. Supporting data: docs/research/hyperliquid-tradexyz-scoping-2026-11-19.md section 3.1 (jurisdiction blocker). Closed by Manager Session 2026-11-22a.
